result.topic_en: Euler applies the boundary conditions for an elastic rod in a second case, derives the ratio alpha/beta and the frequency condition cos ω = 2/(e^ω + e^{-ω}), shows the rod produces the same tones as in the first case, and determines the coefficients, which differ only in the signs of gamma and delta.
result.transcription:
bebimus has aequationes:
$\alpha+\beta+\delta=0$ et $\alpha-\beta+\gamma=0$,
vnde consequimur $\delta=-\alpha-\beta$ et $\gamma=-\alpha+\beta$; posterior vero, quo $s=a$ et $\frac{a}{f}=\omega$, praebet
$\alpha e^{\omega}+\beta e^{-\omega}+\gamma \,\text{fin.}\,\omega+\delta \,\text{cof.}\,\omega=0$ et
$\alpha e^{\omega}-\beta e^{-\omega}+\gamma \,\text{cof.}\,\omega-\delta \,\text{fin.}\,\omega=0$;
vbi si priores valores substituantur, orientur hae aequationes:
$\alpha(e^{\omega}-\text{fin.}\,\omega-\text{cof.}\,\omega)+\beta(e^{-\omega}+\text{fin.}\,\omega-\text{cof.}\,\omega)$ et
$\alpha(e^{\omega}-\text{cof.}\,\omega+\text{fin.}\,\omega)-\beta(e^{-\omega}-\text{cof.}\,\omega-\text{fin.}\,\omega)$;
vnde duplici modo colligitur
$\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{-e^{-\omega}-\text{fin.}\,\omega+\text{cof.}\,\omega}{e^{\omega}-\text{fin.}\,\omega-\text{cof.}\,\omega}=\frac{e^{-\omega}-\text{fin.}\,\omega-\text{cof.}\,\omega}{e^{\omega}+\text{fin.}\,\omega-\text{cof.}\,\omega}$,
qui valores cum prorsus conueniant cum iis, quos casu primo sumus nacti, inde etiam sequitur fore $\text{cof.}\,\omega=\frac{2}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$;
sicque etiam omnes valores anguli $\omega$ iidem erunt, qui primo casu iam sunt exhibiti, scilicet $\omega=\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}, \frac{7\pi}{2}$, etc.
vnde etiam ista virga eosdem edet sonos, qui erunt:
$\frac{9\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{4aa}$; $\frac{25\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{4aa}$; $\frac{49\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{4aa}$; $\frac{81\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{4aa}$; etc.
Praeterea vero etiam erit $\text{fin.}\,\omega=\pm\frac{(e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega})}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$, vbi signum superius valet pro casibus vbi sinus est positiuus, inferius si negatiuus; vnde porro obtinemus $\alpha=1$, $\beta=\mp e^{\omega}$, hincque porro $\gamma=-(1\pm e^{\omega})$ et $\delta=-(1\mp e^{\omega})$. Aequatio igitur pro motu a casu primo in eo tantum differt, quod hic coefficientes $\gamma$ et $\delta$ contraria signa sunt nacti;
T 2
sicque

items.english: from this it also follows that cos ω = 2/(e^ω + e^{-ω}).

items.quote: vnde etiam ista virga eosdem edet sonos
items.english: whence this rod will also produce the same tones.

items.quote: Aequatio igitur pro motu a casu primo in eo tantum differt, quod hic coefficientes $\gamma$ et $\delta$ contraria signa sunt nacti
items.english: The equation for the motion therefore differs from the first case only in that here the coefficients γ and δ have acquired opposite signs.
